title: Recording with King Oliver while with Duke; never under contract
summary: He recorded with Oliver for Clarence Williams after joining Duke, and says he was never under contract to Duke, who could fire him at will as in the early days.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I notice that after you -- According to the discography of the French doctor, you recorded with King Oliver after you were with Duke. How did that come about?
Oh, well, he didn't have any band anymore and I knew the things that he was going to record. He was going to record for Clarence Williams and he asked me to record with him, so I did it.
You see, I was never under no contract
with Duke. I quit when I wanted or if I felt like it. Or he could fire me when he wanted to. It didn't make any difference.
Well, in the early days of the band nobody had any contract or anything.
Harry Carney told me Duke had never gotten around to telling him whether he was permanent or not.
That was kind of the way he dealt in the beginning. Later on I think he occasionally had a contract.
Uh-huh. I don't know what he did later on, but --
